text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Interior Minister Sheikh Mohammad Khaled al-Sabah says Kuwait will devote all available means to combat narcotics.
- Kuwait, Eritrea hold talks on prevention of double taxation.

- Chairman of parliament's Financial and Economic Affairs Committee Nasser al-Sanea says Kuwait's Ministry of Defence did not conclude any sea missile deal. Diplomatic sources say a $150 million order for British Aerospace Plc Sea Skua missiles has been blocked due to parliamentary questions.

- Kuwait wants the final statement by a meeting of the so-called Damascus Declaration to include a clause on Syrian-Iraqi ties improvement. Ministers from the eight Arab member countries of the alliance are currently holding a plenary meeting in Syria. Damascus opened its border with Kuwait's former occupier, Iraq, to trade earlier in June after a closure of some 15 years.
- U.N. arms inspector Rolf Ekeus says Iraq is capable of producing chemical weapons.
- Kuwait's imports from Britain amounted to about $1 billion in 1996.
